summary: Cuts a photo or a video frame into geometric tiles — cells, circles, nested squares. Each tile shows part of the picture, and one number re-rolls the whole layout.
license_note: GPL-3.0-only is the host repo's LICENSE, inherited by this surface rather than chosen for it; the app's own bundled dependencies keep their own licences (React 18, JSZip, pako, mp4-muxer).
origin: Not a git fork (GitHub reports fork=false). Collage Studio arrived on 2026-01-01 as a page of the older nested-resonance-memory-archive. Its source landed first, as a clean save on a public branch; the built app was published to /collage/ the same evening. Where it was written before that save is not recorded in this repo. It inherits the repo's GPL-3.0-only licence rather than choosing one. Its own credits file says it was patterned on the AV Field Toolkit's, and its wishing well was built from the toolkit's too. The app ships React 18, JSZip with pako, and mp4-muxer, plus a small seeded random generator (mulberry32) without a credit line.
origin_audit: Not a git fork (GitHub reports fork=false). Born 2026-01-01 as a surface of the pre-existing nested-resonance-memory-archive, 68 days after that repo's first commit, and the source came FIRST, not the build: a parentless root commit on the public collage-source branch (2af460d8, "Clean save of Smart Crop Collage Source") at 17:51 that evening, 2h24m before the deploy commit that published the built bundle to /collage/ (84a52308, 20:15). This entry asserted the opposite -- build first, source 206 days later -- because both commands behind it read only main's tree while the source sits on a sibling branch that is public right now, and the 2026-07-26 commit that looked like a first arrival is a restore, with all 25 January paths reappearing in it. Since that first commit is parentless and titled a clean save, where Collage Studio was authored BEFORE the import is not recoverable from this repo, and no ATTRIBUTION entry covers it. It inherits GPL-3.0-only from the host repo's LICENSE rather than choosing it, and shares that repo's single Pages artifact and root manifest with AV-TOOLKIT-001. It names one parent itself, in a file it serves to the public: collage/credits.json reads "Isomorphed from av/credits.json, which proved the pattern first." A shipped data file declared the lineage while the manifest at the same origin declared none. The wishing-well runtime flows the same way, from the toolkit to here. Its bundle carries React 18 and react-dom (licence banners survive minification), JSZip 3.10.1 with pako -- which is what makes the .collage project file re-openable -- and mp4-muxer 5.2.2 for the MP4 export, whose handler-box signature survives in the shipped bytes. Its seeded-reroll PRNG (mulberry32) ships unattributed. Measured NEGATIVE worth keeping: no geometry library in a 171-package lockfile and none in the deployed bundle, so the partitioning really is written against the published methods rather than wrapping one.
_note: Per-surface manifest, one of two on this repo's Pages site — the other is /av/wish-it-better.json, and the repo's own stays at the root. It exists because origin (criterion 5 of the Wish It Better network) is a property of each listed surface, not of the repo: Collage Studio and the toolkit have different lineages, and one file copied to both urls could carry only one. Until 2026-08-19 this url served a byte-for-byte copy of the root manifest whose wish_channel was the toolkit's page; the channel is now this page, whose Feedback button opens the shared well (shared/feedback.js) and posts to the same queue as the toolkit's. Level L0, not L1, for the reasons the root manifest records. `origin` here is kept byte-identical by hand to the registry entry COLLAGE-001 in mrdirno/vibe-cards src/site/network.json, because the sweep compares the two; the long record sits under origin_audit and is not compared.
